title: unified-rollouts-proactive-canary-shadow-autorollback-workflows
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve rollout safety by adding proactive autorollback workflows that combine canary, A/B, and shadow traffic probes with multi-metric decisioning. Production incidents show that delayed rollbacks cause higher exposure; this PR implements controller-level probes and policy plumbing to reduce time-to-rollback and make rollouts observable and auditable.

What this change does: Adds a new ProactiveAutoRollback controller that subscribes to rollout events and evaluates configured probe sets (latency, error-rate, hallucination/regression signals) during canary and shadow phases. Introduces a composite metric matcher to support multi-metric thresholds and weighted decisions, and wires rollout events to observability (traces + metrics + rollout audit log). Updates rollout API to accept a "proactiveRollback" block with thresholds, probe windows, and noise-budget parameters.

Design notes: Decisions are made in two tiers: short-window probe (fast failure) and sustained degradation window (confirm). Short-window failures trigger immediate rollback if noise budget exhausted; sustained degradation triggers canary weight reduction and eventual rollback. Shadow traffic probes are non-disruptive and feed into the same decision pipeline. The controller publishes decision rationale to the rollout audit log for post-mortem and metrics ingestion.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add ProactiveAutoRollback controller and reconcile loop
- [x] Implement composite metric matcher and threshold semantics
- [x] Add e2e tests for canary + shadow scenarios
- [x] Emit rollback decision traces and Prometheus metrics
- [x] Update rollout API schema and docs
- [x] Add stability guards to avoid flapping (backoff + cooldown)
- [x] Include migration guide for existing rollout specs

Testing: Unit tests added for policy evaluation and metric matcher (pkg/rollout/autorollback/policy_test.go). e2e tests simulate a canary that ramps to 20% then injects a latency/error regression observed by the probe; controller triggers rollback within configured short window. One e2e initially flakes on CI due to test infra timing; I added a stability guard in e2e harness and re-ran. CI currently green.

Related: ENG-7891 (proactive rollback design), ENG-8023 (observability for rollouts). References to previous work: pr-30211 (metric-driven-rollback), pr-40124 (shadow-canary rollback enhancements).

Migration notes: Old rollout specs without proactiveRollback are unaffected. New fields are additive and optional. For teams that want identical behavior to previous rollouts, set proactiveRollback.disabled=true.

Operational impact: Enables SRE teams to configure shorter probe windows for high-risk models and get faster automatic rollbacks with full audit trail and metrics to evaluate false positives.

review_threads:
Ethan Ross: Overall looks good. Two asks: 1) make short-window default conservative (10s) and configurable; 2) ensure we don't double-count shadow metrics vs canary.
Maya Patel: Set default to 10s and added explicit "source" label to metrics so shadow vs canary are separated in matcher.

Lina Gomez: Please add a unit test for the noise budget decrement path; we had a recent postmortem where noise budget logic was brittle.
Maya Patel: Added policy_test.go covering noise budget decrement and backoff semantics.

Aaron Chu: e2e flake observed on CI; looks like test harness timing assumptions. Consider a retry/backoff.
Maya Patel: Added stability guard and increased tolerances; re-ran e2e and observed stable results.
merge_details: Merged by Lina Gomez using squash-and-merge. Merge commit: f9e8d7c3. Release-note: Adds proactive autorollback workflows for unified rollouts; opt-in via rollout.proactiveRollback. See docs/rollouts/proactive-autorollback.md for configuration and migration steps.
release_notes:
- Add proactive autorollback controller for canary/AB/shadow rollouts.
- New rollout.proactiveRollback schema: thresholds, probe windows, noise budget, cooldowns.
- Emits rollout.rollback_decision metrics and rollout.audit traces.
- Backward compatible: feature is opt-in.
